analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: September core CPI rose 0.33% m/m, above expectations (consensus ~0.20% per the market update). The surprise came partly from shelter: OER rose 0.35% m/m and added about 5bp to core versus GS's forecast.
OER strength was concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68% SA by GS), well above GS's estimate of the underlying trend. Travel services, autos and recreation goods were also firm.
GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.32% m/m, up from its 0.20% pre-CPI expectation, for a y/y rate of +3.09%. The revision reflects upside surprises in OER, hotels and recreation.

SPX fell 1% and NDX fell 2%, the first move of that size since late July. AI-complex sentiment dropped on concern about credit markets' ability to keep financing the AI buildout and on neocloud and hyperscaler bond yields.

Neoclouds fell 12% on the day, a top-5 move in the past 5 years. Other listed AI concerns: OpenAI revenue confusion, China memory breakthroughs easing bottlenecks, datacenter sentiment into the midterms, future power and shell constraints, and further issuance.

After the hot CPI, the market priced a 35% chance of an October hike and 87% for December. GIR still expects a second Fed hike in December and is watching tomorrow's PPI and Fed Chairman Warsh's Bangkok speech.

GS desk activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale and finished 7% better for sale. Asset managers and hedge funds were net sellers on overlapping tech and macro supply. The info tech sell skew was the highest in over 4 weeks.
Major index ETF volumes ran +40-60%, which GS reads as heavy top-down selling.

SEMICON West (Oct 13-14): GS has an incrementally positive view on WFE growth for 2027 and 2028. It estimates 2027 WFE up ~45% y/y to ~$218bn, driven by DRAM, leading-edge foundry/logic and NAND, with 8-10 new fab openings globally.

Leading-edge logic is supported by TSMC 2026 capex of ~$85bn, with additional upside from Intel and Terafab. DRAM spending is strongest as HBM competition drives more capex-intensive solutions. NAND utilization is near peak, and NAND WFE is expected to accelerate into 2027, mostly on technology upgrades.
Test demand is constructive on longer test times for next-generation GPUs and accelerators. Back-end inspection and metrology is constructive on CoWoS and HBM adoption.

Spotify 3Q preview: GS revenue estimate of €4.964bn is modestly below the €5.0bn guidance and slightly below consensus. Premium subscribers of 305mn and MAUs of 788mn are aligned with company targets.

Spotify debate: whether elevated 4Q revenue and gross profit expectations reflect solid subscriber trends and the company's near-term investment cadence. GS modestly lowers 2026 estimates on lower 2H advertising revenue and updated FX rates.

Music industry note: the investor debate has moved from streaming adoption to monetization. The three debates are subscription price increases, monetizing free and ad-supported listening, and the effect of generative AI. GS sees scaled DSPs as relative beneficiaries and a more balanced risk/reward for labels and rights holders.
GS stat of the day: US CPI inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 consecutive months.

tension_points.bull_case: AI datacenter buildouts continue to support robust leading-edge semiconductor investment, with TSMC capex of ~$85bn in 2026 and 2027 WFE seen up ~45% y/y.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit markets and rising hyperscaler bond yields raise doubts about financing the AI trade. Neoclouds fell 12%, with further issuance, power constraints and China memory breakthroughs also cited.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report names no explicit level. The implied checks are a stabilization in hyperscaler and neocloud credit and tomorrow's PPI and Warsh speech, which could move hike pricing.
